title: Cleanup preference initialization
description:
Move some of the preference initialization code around so there doesn't need to be checks checking for initialization, because it should all be done in proper order within epan_init().  proto_pre_init() was created to initialize the tables needed to register "global" (protocol-like) preferences before dissectors themselves have been initialized (and have to register preferences).

Don't have protocols_module be available publicly.

This causes the "Packet Lengths" window (which is a stats tree plugin that uses a UAT preference) to segfault. Still investigating why.

Seems to be "order of operations" issue.  Part of the reason for proto_pre_init() was that preferences were not being initialized "where expected" and what should have be "sanity checks", were actually where preferences were initialized.  Looks like we have a similar issue with how/when UATs are processed.  Prior to this MR, they were being initialized by epan_load_settings() (called from MainApplication::readConfigurationFiles) and NOT part of epan_init (which IMO is where they should be called).
I'm investigating, but if you beat me to it, just add me to the MR.

Found the issue - the "Packet Lengths" UAT is created when the "stat tree" tap listener is created, as part of register_all_tap_listeners(), which is called well after epan_init (which loads the existing 141 UATs).  And since what taps should be registered is application specific, it should be called well after epan_init.  The "stat tree" is the 142nd UAT, but never has its uat_plen_record_post_update_cb() called because it's never (re)loaded because uat_load_all() has already been called.

So I guess where uat_load_all() should be called is the question.

I added uat_load_all() to register_all_tap_listeners() (as a temporary hack) - that fixed the problem, but is ugly.  uat_load_all() has a "loaded" check for each UAT, so it won't reload the 141 previous UATs, but I don't think that's the right solution.
